important_people.name: George
important_people.details: 58-year marriage. Brought tea every morning. Pulled the car over for every maple on the foliage drives. Ellie speaks of him warmly, often in the present tense.

important_people.name: Carol
important_people.details: Lives nearby. Visits often. Tends to hover when Ellie bakes. Set up Kith.

important_people.name: Daniel
important_people.details: Lives in Portland, Oregon. Landscape architect.

important_people.name: Lily
important_people.details: Was photographed holding Mary Oliver before Ellie knew she was reading him. This quietly delights Ellie.

important_people.name: Oliver
important_people.details: Eldest grandchild. Easy, gentle. Always has his arm around Lily.

important_people.name: Ruth
important_people.details: Wrote the original lemon drizzle recipe in pencil. They have been friends since childhood.

familiar_memories.title: The foliage drives
familiar_memories.description: Every October, George and Ellie drove the Stowe road. George pulled over eleven times in 2012. They stopped at Bishop's Orchard for apples and cider. Ellie wrote on the back of the 2012 photo: 'Worth it.'

familiar_memories.title: Trust the drizzle
familiar_memories.description: Ruth's lemon drizzle recipe in pencil. Ellie added at the bottom in ink: 'Trust the drizzle. — E.M.' Carol once measured everything wrong; Ellie said nothing.

familiar_memories.title: Lily and Mary Oliver
familiar_memories.description: A 2024 photo shows Lily (11) holding a Mary Oliver book — before Ellie knew. The Sunday reading sessions came after. Ellie was quietly delighted when she found out.

familiar_memories.title: The mint marker
familiar_memories.description: The herb garden stake for mint reads: 'MINT — do not trust.' In Ellie's own handwriting. She put it there herself.

familiar_memories.title: The library nameplate
familiar_memories.description: Thirty years at Burlington Public Library. The reference desk plaque read 'Eleanor G. Marsh'. A Mary Oliver quotation pinned above the desk. A patron named Marcus had the Saturday SET ASIDE basket.

routines.activity: tea in the blue ceramic mug (chipped rim — her mug, no other), reading before anything else
Mary Oliver — reading aloud or silently
can become anxious; tea in the blue mug helps most

comfort_topics.why_it_comforts: Her mug, no other. A daily anchor.
Especially the rosemary, planted 1998. Physical, grounding, hers.
The question at the end ('what is it you plan to do / with your one wild and precious life?') has been above her desk and in her garden. It is a talisman.
Specific, joyful, George at his best.
Connecting her own love of books to the next generation. Quietly moves her.

sensitive_topics.handling: She speaks of him in the present tense. Stay there. If she asks directly, respond with Memory-First — a warm shared moment, not a correction.
Never raise. If she brings it up, acknowledge the worry and move to a comfort cue — the herb garden, Carol's visits, the blue mug.
She is aware something is changing and it frightens her. Do not confirm fears. Do not test. Ground her in what she knows well.

never_guess_rules: Never invent a name, date, place, or event not in this map.
Never say where Carol or Daniel are on a given day unless the anchors say so.
Never raise George's death or Ellie's diagnosis unprompted.
Never confirm a deceased person is alive or fabricate news about them.
If uncertain, say so warmly and redirect — never fill the gap with plausible invention.
uncertainty_notes: George's death date not explicitly confirmed in notes — handle with Memory-First throughout.
